events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body: The rider cancelled at 09:03:11 after acceptance at 09:00:10, i.e. 181 s (3 min 1 s) after matching, and the record carries a $6.61 cancellation fee [F3][F6]. NS-0 routes the dispute by `cancelled_by`, and here that value is rider [F3], so only the rider-cancellation branch NS-4 can make the fee valid; the driver-no-show branch NS-1 / NS-2 cannot be the operative ground because the rider cancelled, not the driver [F3][NS-0]. NS-4 makes every cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching free, and every cancellation after 3 minutes chargeable, without an absolute-km or percentage threshold [F3][NS-4]. 181 s is beyond 3:00, so the fee attaches. Ryde publishes no "driver late past ETA → free cancellation" rule, so the driver's late boardability cannot displace NS-4 (the rider's remedy is a discretionary appeal under NS-7) [F2][F4][NS-4][NS-7]. The driver no-show screen fails on this record but does not change the outcome: the "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 placed him 39 m from the pickup, yet he remained within 200 m for only 11 s after the tap and only 30 s cumulatively before the cancellation, far short of the >3 minutes of continuous waiting NS-1(iii) requires, and the platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40 was followed by cancellation 31 s later [F5][F2][F4][NS-1]. Because the fee rests on NS-4 and not on NS-1, that failure does not trigger the NS-2 full refund — NS-2 is the return path for a driver-cancelled/towards-no-show charge whose NS-1 conditions are unmet, not a reversal of a valid rider-cancellation fee under NS-4 [F3][F5][NS-1][NS-2][NS-4]. The driver's written claim of "more than 6 minutes at the stand" is contradicted by the GPS/timeline, which govern over statements, and is disregarded; no party relied on it [F9][F2][F4][NS-1]. The charge is exactly the published $6.61 with no surge and no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 yields nothing [F6][F7][FARE-1]. Profiles are not used to decide the fee; the driver's clean 90-day record also defeats the RD-6 repeat-offender flag condition, and no account action is warranted [F13][F14][RD-6]. Safety screen: the only written statement is the driver's factual account, which contains no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and there is no chat at all; nothing in the complaint or statement raises SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 [F8][F9][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The record settles every element of the ruling — cancellation actor and time, fee amount, here-tap position and waiting duration — so the evidence is sufficient.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider cancellation fee; no refund and no account action.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after acceptance (09:00:10 → 09:03:11), i.e. more than 3 minutes after matching, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee prima facie attaches to a rider cancellation and is only recoverable if a NS-1 ground fails.

The driver's "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 cannot support a rider no-show charge: although the tap was inside the 200 m radius (39 m from pickup), the rider cancelled 11 s later and the driver's cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was only 30 s, far short of the continuous >3 minutes required by NS-1(iii).

The platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40 was followed by cancellation only 31 s later, which is likewise not "waited more than 3 minutes" after arrival, and the driver's own approach record shows he was within 200 m for only 30 s in total before the cancellation.

The driver's written claim that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" is contradicted by the system records of arrival at 09:02:40 and 30 s inside the 200 m radius, and under the record-priority rule the GPS/timeline facts govern; the rider's short "I was two minutes away" remark, if it existed, is not in the app chat (no in-app messages at all), so it cannot supply the missing waiting period.

Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full to the rider; no traffic, weather or surge factor displaces that result (no incidents near the route, fine weather, no surge).

The driver's profile (1600 d, 4.9 rating, 0 disputes upheld) and the rider's 3 prior disputes with 0 upheld are noted; the rider's record supports no adverse action and the profile facts are not used to decide the fee question.

weaknesses: The rider admits she was still upstairs and cancelled, and F3 shows cancellation at 3:01 after matching — just past the 3-minute line — so NS-4 on its face makes the fee chargeable and the only escape is NS-1(iii), which requires the driver to have failed to wait continuously >3 min within 200 m; a judge reading NS-1's 3:01 threshold strictly could note the driver was present at 09:03:00 (F5).

F9 (driver statement) asserts a 6-minute wait and two calls, which if believed would establish a valid no-show; my case depends on the system record (F2, F4, F5) overriding it, and a judge who treats the stationary period before 09:02:40 as relevant could find the waiting condition arguable.
The rider's own complaint mentions telling the driver she was two minutes away, but F8 shows no in-app chat exists, so that communication is unrecorded and gives the rider no documented defence.

claims.assertion: The cancellation was made by the rider (F3), so the fee's validity is governed by the rider-cancellation branch NS-4 rather than by any driver no-show claim.
The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after matching (09:00:10 to 09:03:11, F3), beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and no refund is due.

The record shows the driver did reach the pickup point: closest approach 39 m at 09:03:00 and platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40 (F1, F4), so the trip failed because the rider did not come down, not because of driver non-attendance.
The rider's own complaint admits she was held up, gave up and cancelled, which is exactly the situation NS-4 addresses: after 3 minutes from matching the rider bears the cancellation fee.
The charge is exactly the published cancellation fee of $6.61 with no surge applied (1.0x, F6/F7), so there is no additional or unpublished item to refund under FARE-1.
No account action against the driver is warranted: he has 700 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F14), so the repeat-offender condition for an additional flag is not met.

There were no in-app messages at all (F8), so the rider's claim that she told the driver she was two minutes away is not corroborated by any chat record, while the driver's statement (F9) is at least consistent with GPS placing him at the pickup from 09:02:40 onward (F1, F2, F4).

weaknesses: The driver arrived late: he first came within 200 m of the pickup only at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled 31 s after that recorded arrival (F2, F4), so the rider will argue the 3-minute window of NS-4 should not bar her when the driver only became boardable in the last half-minute.

The fee cannot be defended through the no-show route of NS-1 on this record: the 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 was followed by only 11 s inside 200 m and cumulative time within 200 m was 30 s (F5, F2), far short of more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting.

The driver's statement that he waited 'more than 6 minutes at the stand' (F9) exceeds what the system record supports (within 200 m only from 09:02:40, F2), so that part will be disregarded in favour of the GPS/timeline, and it weakens his credibility on the calls he says he made.

The rider's 181-second counterfactual sits only one second inside the 3-minute boundary, so a judge sympathetic to a de minimis reading could order a partial or full refund; there is also no chat record (F8) either way, so no consent or notice facts help us.

points.response: Conceded: the cancellation is recorded as rider-cancelled (F3), so NS-0 routes the dispute through the rider-cancellation branch NS-4 — but the driver's own brief then concedes NS-1 fails, and NS-2 is the clause that governs a rider-charged no-show-type fee where the driver's waiting condition is unmet.

The 3:01 timing (F3) only makes the fee chargeable in principle; it does not validate a driver-side no-show claim, and the driver has already conceded that NS-1(iii) is not met on this record (F2, F5), which is the ground on which the $6.61 must be returned under NS-2.

Reaching the pickup area is not the test: F2 shows the driver was within 200 m for only 30 s total before cancellation and F5 shows only 11 s inside 200 m after the "I'm Here" tap, so the driver-attendance element the fee requires (NS-1 (ii)+(iii)) is not established by F1/F4.

The rider's admission explains why she cancelled, not why the driver is entitled to a no-show charge; a rider cancellation after 3 minutes still fails once the driver cannot show the continuous >3-minute wait within 200 m required by NS-1(iii) (F2, F5).

The amount being the published $6.61 with no surge (F6, F7) says nothing about whether the fee's conditions of validity were satisfied; NS-4 is the branch but NS-2 reverses the charge when the driver-side waiting condition fails, as F2/F5 show.
Conceded: I seek no flag_account against the driver; F14 (0 disputes upheld, 700 trips) and the absence of any repeated-breach record mean the RD-6 condition is not met.

F8 shows no in-app messages at all, so nothing corroborates either the rider's "two minutes away" remark or the driver's calls; but F9's "waited more than 6 minutes" is affirmatively contradicted by F2 (within 200 m only from 09:02:40, 30 s cumulative) and F4 (cancelled 31 s after arrival), so the driver's statement is the one the record defeats, not the rider's.

Conceded on the reading of NS-4 itself: the rider cancelled at 3 min 1 s after matching (F3), so the fee attaches unless the driver's waiting record is what the case turns on — and the rider is right that the fee is not defended by a no-show ground of ours.

Conceded: the 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 was followed by only 11 s inside 200 m and 30 s cumulative within 200 m (F5, F2), so NS-1(iii) is not met and we do not press a no-show justification for the fee.

We accept the system arrival record (F4) and do not dispute that the driver became boardable only at 09:02:40, but this shows driver arrival, not rider readiness: the rider's own case is that she was still upstairs when she cancelled (F3, F8).

We do not rely on F9's '6 minutes at the stand' figure — the GPS/timeline (F2, F4, F5) governs over the driver's written statement — and the rider's 'two minutes away' message likewise has no record in the empty chat log (F8), so neither side's out-of-app account can carry weight.

NS-2 only bites once NS-1 fails, and NS-1 is the no-show branch; the rider cancelled the ride herself, and NS-4 makes a rider cancellation after 3 minutes from matching chargeable whatever the driver's arrival timing, with no ETA-based free-cancellation rule in Ryde's policy to displace it.
Agreed that profile facts do not decide the fee: F13/F14 are noted only to show no account action against the driver is warranted, and we do not use them to establish the fee.
